data.title: Chat: link-sites guard — template-literal keys and a second .href assignment inside one statement are invisible to T8/T9

data.body: Filed from the AS-120 review (agent:qa-priya, M6 probes past the list; neither item violates an AS-120 or AS-98 stated criterion, neither is an honest-mistake idiom — backlog, not a blocker). Reproduce with scratchpad/agent-qa-priya/AS-120/probe.mjs against link-sites.test.js at 889a566. (1) Quote class: MECHANISMS matches setAttribute\(\s*['"]href['"] and \[\s*['"]href['"]\s*\] — single/double quotes only. open[`href`] = x and open.setAttribute(`href`, x) are count 0 / no mechanism hit: T8 blind, T9 blind. Fix: add the backtick to both character classes (["'`]) and a T11-style rejected input for each; T12-style self-test. (2) RHS capture [^;\n]* swallows a second .href assignment in the same statement: a.href = dashHref(x), b.href = task.taskId; and cond ? (a.href = dashHref(x)) : (b.href = task.taskId); both classify as count 1 with zero violations because the first RHS begins with an allowlisted source. Fix options: split the RHS head at ',' / ')' before allowlist matching, or count .href<op> tokens separately from RHS classification so the count pin still moves. Observed-adversarial, recorded as boundary in the AS-120 review: comments/whitespace inside the member expression (a.href /* */ = x, a . href = x) and setAttributeNode(createAttribute('href')) — same lexical-guard class as AS-98 §1.4, listed here for the record, not necessarily in scope for this task.
